object.title: UU-AAP Core v0.1 Receipt Chain Validator
object.description: Russian software-registration object: the standalone Node.js validator for machine-readable UU-AAP Core v0.1 receipt chains, with its receipt-envelope schema and conformance fixture as identifying/deposit-support material. Abstract protocol ideas, CCRP, KONTUR, PoAI and unrelated implementations are outside this Wave 1 software object. Potentially patentable technical mechanisms are handled independently in patent-track issue #492.

authors.name: private-party:wave1-declarant-01
authors.contribution_scope: Selected Wave 1 Core validator surface. Human contribution is classified as AI-assisted human creation: architecture choices, personal source development, material restructuring, algorithmic choices, validation checks and audit-driven integration. This does not claim every AI-generated token as independently human-authored.

right_holders.name: private-party:wave1-declarant-01
right_holders.contribution_scope: Selected Wave 1 Core validator surface only. Declarant reports no employment-duty allocation, customer/commission allocation, exclusive-right assignment, coauthor claim or incorporated third-party protected expression affecting this scope.

patentability.reviewer_or_authority: UU-AAP Wave 1 evidence-bound screen; technical patent review tracked separately in issue #492
patentability.notes: For Wave 1, the filing object is the concrete program expression and identifying materials only. The Core surface is already public. The software-registration path makes no patent claim and does not classify underlying UU-AAP technical mechanisms as non-patentable. Those mechanisms remain subject to separate novelty, technical-character, inventorship and disclosure review in issue #492, including the 2027 Russian programmable-means amendments.

registration_intent.rationale: Create an official registry record for one coherent, rights-cleared executable UU-AAP Core validator while preserving a separate patent track for potentially technical mechanisms and the distinction between protected software expression and abstract architecture.
